subject: ISLAMIC RELIGIOUS EDUCATION
title: Belief in Angels
overview: Belief in the angels is a pillar of Iman. Angels are honoured creatures of Allah who never disobey Him. In this sub-strand you will name Jibril, Mikail, Raqib and Atid, Malakul Maut (Izrail) and Israfil, and you will learn the duty of each.

lessons.title: Angels and the pillar of Iman
objectives: State that belief in angels is a pillar of Iman.
Describe what Muslims believe about angels as Allah’s creation.
lessons.intro: You cannot see them arranging the rows of a lesson, yet a Muslim believes they are real. The angels are a creation of Allah, and believing in them is one of the pillars of Iman.
lessons.notes:
### A pillar of faith
Iman includes belief in Allah, His angels, His books, His messengers, the Last Day, and the decree of good and evil. Belief in the angels is the second of these pillars. A person who denies the angels has left this pillar out of faith.

### What angels are
Angels are created by Allah. A Hadith in Sahih Muslim says that the angels were created from light. They do not eat, drink or sleep as people do. They do not disobey Allah, and they do what He commands (Qur’an 66:6). They worship Him constantly. They are not the sons or daughters of Allah, and it is forbidden to worship them. We respect them because Allah created them and gave them duties.

We do not usually see them in their true form. Jibril (alayhis-salam) sometimes came to the Prophet (S.A.W.) in the form of a man. Their real nature is known through revelation, not through guessing.

### The angels you will name
In this sub-strand the selected angels are:

- Jibril
- Mikail
- Raqib and Atid
- Malakul Maut (Izrail)
- Israfil

Learn to pronounce each name. Later lessons will join each name to a duty. For now, be able to list them and to say why a Muslim believes in them: Allah has told us about them, and belief in them is part of Iman. Appreciating them begins by accepting that they are real, honoured, and busy with Allah’s command.

keyWords.meaning: a creature of light who obeys Allah and carries out His commands
one of the main beliefs that faith stands on

examples.problem: A classmate says, “I will believe in angels only when I see one.” What should a Muslim answer?
steps: Belief in the unseen, including angels, is part of Iman.
Allah has informed us of them in the Qur’an and through the Prophet (S.A.W.).
Not seeing them does not mean they are absent.
examples.answer: A Muslim believes in the angels because Allah has told us about them, even though we do not see them in their true form.

activity.title: Name the selected angels
steps: Listen to the teacher say: Jibril, Mikail, Raqib, Atid, Izrail (Malakul Maut) and Israfil.
Repeat the names until the group can say them in order.
Write the names in your notebook under the heading “Angels I believe in”.
Tell a partner why belief in angels is a pillar of Iman.

practice.question: Name the selected angels in this sub-strand.
practice.answer: Jibril, Mikail, Raqib and Atid, Malakul Maut (Izrail) and Israfil.

practice.question: From what were the angels created, according to the Hadith in Sahih Muslim?
Do angels disobey Allah?
practice.answer: No. They do what Allah commands.

summary: Belief in the angels is a pillar of Iman.
Angels are created from light, and they do not disobey Allah.
The selected angels are Jibril, Mikail, Raqib, Atid, Izrail and Israfil.

lessons.title: Jibril and Mikail
objectives: Show why these duties matter in a Muslim’s life.
lessons.intro: The Qur’an you recite reached the Prophet (S.A.W.) through an angel. The rain that grows maize is also under an angel’s duty, by Allah’s command. Those two angels are Jibril and Mikail.
lessons.notes:
### Jibril (alayhis-salam)
Jibril is the angel of revelation. He brought Allah’s words to the prophets. He brought the Qur’an to Prophet Muhammad (S.A.W.). The first revelation came to the Prophet while he was in the cave of Hira, when Jibril came to him. Jibril is also called Ruh al-Qudus, the Holy Spirit, in the Qur’an, in the sense of this pure angel, not in any other meaning. Muslims send peace on him when they mention him: alayhis-salam.

Because of Jibril’s duty, we have the Qur’an to recite in swalah. Every time you read Al-Fatiha, you are using a message that Allah sent by this angel. Love of the Qur’an is a way of appreciating that duty.

### Mikail (alayhis-salam)
Mikail is entrusted with rain and with provision, rizq, by Allah’s command. Crops, rivers and the food on a plate are not accidents. Allah provides, and He has given Mikail this duty. The Qur’an mentions Mikail among those whom a believer must not take as an enemy (Qur’an 2:98).

### What this means for you
When rain falls, thank Allah, and remember that His angel carries out the command. When you recite Qur’an, thank Allah for sending Jibril to the Prophet (S.A.W.). Do not worship either angel. Thankfulness belongs to Allah, who created them and who sends both revelation and rain.

keyWords.meaning: the angel who brought revelation to the prophets
the angel entrusted with rain and provision

examples.problem: During a drought a learner says, “Rain has nothing to do with faith.” How do you answer using the duty of Mikail, without forgetting Allah?
steps: Allah is the Provider.
Mikail is entrusted with rain and provision by Allah’s command.
The learner should make dua to Allah for rain and thank Him when it comes.
examples.answer: Allah sends provision, and Mikail carries out the duty of rain by His command. We ask Allah, not the angel.

activity.title: Match Jibril and Mikail with their duties
materials: Flash cards of names and duties
steps: Place the name cards Jibril and Mikail on the desk.
Match them with the duty cards: revelation, and rain and provision.
In pairs, explain why each duty matters to a Grade 4 learner.
Write two sentences in your notebook, one for each angel.

practice.question: What is the duty of Jibril?
practice.answer: He brings Allah’s revelation to the prophets. He brought the Qur’an to Prophet Muhammad (S.A.W.).

practice.question: What is the duty of Mikail?
practice.answer: He is entrusted with rain and provision by Allah’s command.

practice.question: Should a Muslim worship Jibril because he brought the Qur’an?
practice.answer: No. Worship is for Allah alone. Jibril obeys Allah.

summary: Jibril brought revelation, including the Qur’an, to the Prophet (S.A.W.).
Mikail is entrusted with rain and provision.
We thank Allah for both duties and we do not worship the angels.

lessons.title: Raqib, Atid, Izrail and Israfil
objectives: Explain the duties of Raqib and Atid.
Explain the duties of Malakul Maut and Israfil.
Match each selected angel with the correct duty.
lessons.intro: Two angels write what you say and do. Another will take the soul when the appointed time comes. Another will blow the trumpet that begins the Day of Judgement. Their names are part of a Muslim’s faith.
lessons.notes:
### Raqib and Atid
Raqib and Atid are the recording angels who stay with every person. The Qur’an speaks of two receivers, one on the right and one on the left, and says that a person does not utter a word without an observer ready (Qur’an 50:17-18). It also speaks of noble scribes who record what people do (Qur’an 82:10-12). One records good deeds and the other records bad deeds. Nothing of that record is lost.

### Malakul Maut (Izrail)
Malakul Maut means the Angel of Death. The Qur’an says the angel of death will take the souls (Qur’an 32:11). He is also called Izrail in Islamic teaching. He takes a soul only when Allah has appointed that time. He does not act by his own wish. Remembering him should push a learner to obey Allah, not to tell frightening stories or to be cruel.

### Israfil
Israfil will blow the trumpet. The Qur’an describes a blast after which those in the heavens and the earth fall unconscious, except whom Allah wills, and a later blast after which they stand, looking (Qur’an 39:68). The first blast brings the end of this world as we know it, and the next blast is the resurrection for judgement.

Learn the four duties until you can match them without the chart: recorders, Angel of Death, and the angel of the trumpet. These duties are signs that this life is written, that it will end, and that it will be judged.

keyWords.meaning: the two angels who record a person’s deeds
the Angel of Death, who takes souls by Allah’s command
the angel who will blow the trumpet

examples.problem: Sort these duties under the right names: blowing the trumpet, taking the soul, writing good and bad deeds.
steps: Israfil blows the trumpet.
Malakul Maut (Izrail) takes the soul at the appointed time.
Raqib and Atid record the deeds.
examples.answer: Israfil: the trumpet. Izrail: the soul. Raqib and Atid: the record of deeds.

activity.title: Angel crossword and matching cards
materials: A simple crossword or word search with the six names
steps: In pairs, find the names Jibril, Mikail, Raqib, Atid, Izrail and Israfil in the puzzle.
Match each name card with its duty card on the pocket board or desk.
Check another pair and correct any mismatch.
Write the full list of names and duties in your notebook.

practice.question: What do Raqib and Atid do?
practice.answer: They record a person’s deeds. One records good deeds and the other records bad deeds.

practice.question: Who is Malakul Maut, and what is his duty?
practice.answer: He is the Angel of Death, also called Izrail. He takes souls when Allah has appointed the time.

practice.question: What will Israfil do?
practice.answer: He will blow the trumpet for the events of the Last Day, as the Qur’an describes.

practice.question: Which Qur’an reference speaks of the two receivers who record words?

summary: Raqib and Atid record good and bad deeds.
Izrail, the Angel of Death, takes souls by Allah’s command.

lessons.title: Living with belief in the angels
objectives: Explain how the duties of the angels affect daily choices.
Show appreciation for the angels as Allah’s creation.
Use a class qasida to remember names and duties.
lessons.intro: Belief in the recording angels should make a person careful, not hopeless. A good word is written, and a bad word is written. This lesson turns that knowledge into careful speech and hopeful deeds.
lessons.notes:
### Why Allah created the angels
Allah created the angels to worship Him and to carry out His commands. Their duties serve His wisdom: revelation is delivered, provision is managed by His leave, deeds are recorded, souls are taken at the right time, and the trumpet will be blown when He wills. They are a sign of His power and of His care for the universe.

### What their duties mean for a learner
- Because Jibril brought the Qur’an, we recite it respectfully and follow it.
- Because Mikail’s duty concerns rain and rizq, we thank Allah for food and we do not waste it.
- Because Raqib and Atid write our deeds, we choose words and actions we would be happy to see in the record. A kind word is worth saying. A lie is not worth the line it will fill.
- Because Izrail will take the soul at an appointed time, we do not delay a good deed as if we owned tomorrow.
- Because Israfil will blow the trumpet, we believe the Day of Judgement is real and we prepare for it.

### Appreciation
We appreciate the angels by believing in them, speaking of them with respect, and refusing jokes that insult them. We do not draw them as we imagine, and we do not worship them. A class qasida can help memory: “Jibril brought the Book we read, Mikail brings the rain we need, Raqib and Atid write the deed, Izrail calls the soul, Israfil’s trumpet wakes the world, by Allah’s leave alone.” Use the song to remember, and use your behaviour to show that the belief is alive.

keyWords.meaning: the writing of good and bad actions kept by the recording angels
to value the angels by believing in them and respecting them

examples.problem: Two learners start to mock a classmate with a rude nickname. One of them remembers Raqib and Atid. What changes?
steps: The words would be recorded.
He stops the nickname and says a kind word instead.
The kind word is also recorded.
examples.answer: He stops the insult because it would be written, and he chooses a good word that will be written instead.

activity.title: Qasida and a notebook of duties
materials: Digital device to find a suitable qasida with the teacher, or the class lines above
steps: With the teacher, listen to or sing a qasida on the angels and their duties. If no suitable recording is available, learn the class lines.
In pairs, brainstorm how each duty touches your life and write five points.
Share one point with the class and listen respectfully to other opinions.
Copy the corrected points into your notebook.

practice.question: Why did Allah create the angels?
practice.answer: To worship Him and to carry out His commands.

practice.question: How should belief in Raqib and Atid change a learner’s speech?
practice.answer: The learner avoids lies and insults because they are recorded, and chooses good words that are also recorded.

practice.question: Give two ways of appreciating the angels without worshipping them.
practice.answer: Believe in them, speak of them with respect, follow the Qur’an Jibril brought, and thank Allah for the duties they carry out.

summary: Angels worship Allah and carry out His commands.
Their duties encourage careful speech, thankfulness, and preparation for the Last Day.
We respect angels and we worship Allah alone.
